**Rachael May Taylor** (born 11 July 1984) is an Australian actress and model. She began her career as a model before transitioning to acting, gaining early recognition for the Australian television series _headLand_ (2005–2006). She subsequently appeared in the films _Man-Thing_ (2005), _See No Evil_ (2006), _Transformers_ (2007), _Bottle Shock_ (2008), _Shutter_ (2008), _Cedar Boys_ (2009), _Splinterheads_ (2009), _Red Dog_ (2011), _The Darkest Hour_ (2011) and _Any Questions for Ben?_ (2012).
Taylor is best known for portraying Trish Walker in the Marvel Cinematic Universe television series _Jessica Jones_ (2015–2019), _Luke Cage_ (2016) and _The Defenders_ (2017). She also portrayed [Dr. Lucy Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Grey's_Anatomy_characters#Attending_physicians "List of Grey's Anatomy characters") on _[Grey's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey's\_Anatomy "Grey's Anatomy")_ (2011), an Angel in _[Charlie's Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie's\_Angels\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Charlie's Angels (2011 TV series)")_ (2011), Jane Van Veen in _666 Park Avenue_ (2012–2013) and Susie Dunn in the NBC action/thriller series _Crisis_ (2014).

Rachael May Taylor[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-2) was born on 11 July 1984 in Launceston, Tasmania.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3) Her English parents, Christine and Nigel Taylor, emigrated from Dorset and Lancashire respectively and met in Tasmania.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-5)
Taylor attended Trevallyn Primary School and Riverside High School._[citation needed_] She moved to Sydney at the age of 16 to become an actress, though later returned to Launceston to complete her high school education.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4) She studied history and politics at the University of Sydney before leaving in 2006.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3)
Taylor modelled as a teenager, and reached the state finals of Miss Teen Tasmania and Miss Universe/Miss World.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3) In 1998, she won the title of Miss Teen Tasmania.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4) She stated in 2015: "I don't think that was a particularly healthy environment for a 14-year-old. I think women are asked to consider their beauty too much."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4)

She made her acting debut in _The Mystery of Natalie Wood_, a 2004 television serial directed by Peter Bogdanovich.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-mercury-6) She appeared in a number of American productions – such as the television film _Dynasty: The Making of a Guilty Pleasure_ (2005) (where she played Catherine Oxenberg),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-Dynasty-7)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-mercury-6) and the horror movies_Man-Thing_ (2005) and _See No Evil_ (2006).
Taylor played Sasha Forbes on the short-lived Australian drama series _headLand_. On 3 April 2006, she was nominated for a Logie Award for Most Popular New Female Talent for her role on _headLand_.
Taylor at the premiere of _Transformers_ in Sydney, 2007
Her most prominent role to date was as Maggie Madsen, a signals analyst, in the 2007 _Transformers_, where she appeared alongside Shia LaBeouf and Megan Fox. Taylor confirmed that she would not be returning for the _Transformers_ sequel.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-8) In 2008, Taylor scored a starring role in the US horror-thriller _Shutter_, a remake of the 2004 Thai film of the same name opposite Joshua Jackson.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-9) Despite mixed reviews, the film was a box-office success.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-10)

In 2009, she completed the Australian feature _Cedar Boys_ and starred in the comedy _Splinterheads_. In 2010, she starred alongside Alex Dimitriades in the Australian romantic drama _Summer Coda_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-11) She has also signed to the HBO comedy series _Washingtonienne_ and _Melt_, an Australian production. Taylor began a recurring role on _[Grey's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey's\_Anatomy "Grey's Anatomy")_ as [Dr. Lucy Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Grey's_Anatomy_characters#Attending_physicians "List of Grey's Anatomy characters"), an obstetrician and maternal-fetal fellow.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-14)
In 2011, Taylor joined the cast of the short-lived remake of the television series _[Charlie's Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie's\_Angels\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Charlie's Angels (2011 TV series)")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-16) Also in 2011, she had a major role in the film _Red Dog_ and starred in the Russian science-fiction thriller film _The Darkest Hour_, directed by filmmaker Chris Gorak.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-17)

**Laura Haddock** (born 1985) is a British actress. She is known for portraying Alison in _The Inbetweeners Movie_, Zoë Walker in _White Lines_, Max Meladze in _The Recruit_, Lucrezia in _[Da Vinci's Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da\_Vinci's\_Demons "Da Vinci's Demons")_, Meredith Quill in _Guardians of the Galaxy_ and its sequel _Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2_, and Viviane Wembly in _Transformers: The Last Knight_.

## Early life and education
[edit]
Laura Haddock was born in 1985[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-1) in Enfield, London, to a reflexologist mother and a financier father.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-2) She was raised in Harpenden, Hertfordshire.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-Times1-3)
She attended [St George's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_George's_School,_Harpenden "St George's School, Harpenden") in Harpenden.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-Times1-3) She left school at the age of 17 and moved to London to study drama. She trained at Arts Educational School in Chiswick.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-OK1-4)
Haddock made her television debut in the television pilot_Plus One_, part of the Comedy Showcase 2008.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-5) In 2009, Haddock played the lead role of Natasha in the ITV1comedy drama_Monday Monday_, and appeared as Samantha in series two and three of _How Not to Live Your Life_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-ITV1-6)

## Early life and education
In 2011, she appeared in the Cinemax/Sky TV drama _Strike Back: Project Dawn_ for two episodes, as the kidnapped daughter of an illegal arms dealer. She starred as Lucrezia Donati,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-Cast-7) the mistress of [Lorenzo de' Medici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenzo_de'_Medici "Lorenzo de' Medici") and lover of Leonardo da Vinci in the 2013 series _[Da Vinci's Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da\_Vinci's\_Demons "Da Vinci's Demons")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-8) She played Alison, Will McKenzie's love interest, in _The Inbetweeners Movie_ (2011),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-9) for which she was nominated for the Empire Award for Best Female Newcomer.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-10)
Haddock's theatre credits include _Famous Last_, which formed part of the 2009 Sky Arts Theatre Live! project,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-SkyArts-11) and _Rutherford & Son_ at Northern Stage.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-WOS1-12) In 2014, she portrayed Meredith Quill in _Guardians of the Galaxy_, a role she reprised in its 2017 sequel _Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2_. She appears in the ITV series, _The Level_, and played Vivian Wembley in the 2017 film _Transformers: The Last Knight_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-13)

## Early life and education
In 2021, Haddock starred in a Christmas marketing campaign for British furniture and home accessories retailer OKA.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-ver1-14) In 2022, she starred as Maxine Meladze in the Netflix spy-adventure television series _The Recruit_.
Haddock married English actor Sam Claflin in July 2013 after dating for two years.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-15) They have a son and a daughter.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-16) On 20 August 2019, Haddock and Claflin announced their legal separation.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-18)

Rachael May Taylor[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-2) was born on 11 July 1984 in Launceston, Tasmania.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3) Her English parents, Christine and Nigel Taylor, emigrated from Dorset and Lancashire respectively and met in Tasmania.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-5)
Taylor attended Trevallyn Primary School and Riverside High School._[citation needed_] She moved to Sydney at the age of 16 to become an actress, though later returned to Launceston to complete her high school education.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4) She studied history and politics at the University of Sydney before leaving in 2006.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3)
Taylor modelled as a teenager, and reached the state finals of Miss Teen Tasmania and Miss Universe/Miss World.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3) In 1998, she won the title of Miss Teen Tasmania.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4) She stated in 2015: "I don't think that was a particularly healthy environment for a 14-year-old. I think women are asked to consider their beauty too much."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4)
texts.2:
She made her acting debut in _The Mystery of Natalie Wood_, a 2004 television serial directed by Peter Bogdanovich.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-mercury-6) She appeared in a number of American productions – such as the television film _Dynasty: The Making of a Guilty Pleasure_ (2005) (where she played Catherine Oxenberg),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-Dynasty-7)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-mercury-6) and the horror movies_Man-Thing_ (2005) and _See No Evil_ (2006).
Taylor played Sasha Forbes on the short-lived Australian drama series _headLand_. On 3 April 2006, she was nominated for a Logie Award for Most Popular New Female Talent for her role on _headLand_.
Taylor at the premiere of _Transformers_ in Sydney, 2007
Her most prominent role to date was as Maggie Madsen, a signals analyst, in the 2007 _Transformers_, where she appeared alongside Shia LaBeouf and Megan Fox. Taylor confirmed that she would not be returning for the _Transformers_ sequel.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-8) In 2008, Taylor scored a starring role in the US horror-thriller _Shutter_, a remake of the 2004 Thai film of the same name opposite Joshua Jackson.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-9) Despite mixed reviews, the film was a box-office success.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-10)

**Laura Haddock** (born 1985) is a British actress. She is known for portraying Alison in _The Inbetweeners Movie_, Zoë Walker in _White Lines_, Max Meladze in _The Recruit_, Lucrezia in _[Da Vinci's Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da\_Vinci's\_Demons "Da Vinci's Demons")_, Meredith Quill in _Guardians of the Galaxy_ and its sequel _Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2_, and Viviane Wembly in _Transformers: The Last Knight_.
texts.1:
## Early life and education
[edit]
Laura Haddock was born in 1985[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-1) in Enfield, London, to a reflexologist mother and a financier father.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-2) She was raised in Harpenden, Hertfordshire.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-Times1-3)
She attended [St George's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_George's_School,_Harpenden "St George's School, Harpenden") in Harpenden.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-Times1-3) She left school at the age of 17 and moved to London to study drama. She trained at Arts Educational School in Chiswick.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-OK1-4)
Haddock made her television debut in the television pilot_Plus One_, part of the Comedy Showcase 2008.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-5) In 2009, Haddock played the lead role of Natasha in the ITV1comedy drama_Monday Monday_, and appeared as Samantha in series two and three of _How Not to Live Your Life_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-ITV1-6)
texts.2:
## Early life and education
In 2011, she appeared in the Cinemax/Sky TV drama _Strike Back: Project Dawn_ for two episodes, as the kidnapped daughter of an illegal arms dealer. She starred as Lucrezia Donati,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-Cast-7) the mistress of [Lorenzo de' Medici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenzo_de'_Medici "Lorenzo de' Medici") and lover of Leonardo da Vinci in the 2013 series _[Da Vinci's Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da\_Vinci's\_Demons "Da Vinci's Demons")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-8) She played Alison, Will McKenzie's love interest, in _The Inbetweeners Movie_ (2011),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-9) for which she was nominated for the Empire Award for Best Female Newcomer.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-10)
Haddock's theatre credits include _Famous Last_, which formed part of the 2009 Sky Arts Theatre Live! project,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-SkyArts-11) and _Rutherford & Son_ at Northern Stage.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-WOS1-12) In 2014, she portrayed Meredith Quill in _Guardians of the Galaxy_, a role she reprised in its 2017 sequel _Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2_. She appears in the ITV series, _The Level_, and played Vivian Wembley in the 2017 film _Transformers: The Last Knight_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-13)
texts.3:
## Early life and education
In 2021, Haddock starred in a Christmas marketing campaign for British furniture and home accessories retailer OKA.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-ver1-14) In 2022, she starred as Maxine Meladze in the Netflix spy-adventure television series _The Recruit_.
Haddock married English actor Sam Claflin in July 2013 after dating for two years.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-15) They have a son and a daughter.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-16) On 20 August 2019, Haddock and Claflin announced their legal separation.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-18)

Taylor attended Trevallyn Primary School and Riverside High School._[citation needed_] She moved to Sydney at the age of 16 to become an actress, though later returned to Launceston to complete her high school education.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4) She studied history and politics at the University of Sydney before leaving in 2006.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3)
Taylor modelled as a teenager, and reached the state finals of Miss Teen Tasmania and Miss Universe/Miss World.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3) In 1998, she won the title of Miss Teen Tasmania.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4) She stated in 2015: "I don't think that was a particularly healthy environment for a 14-year-old. I think women are asked to consider their beauty too much."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-:1-4)

She made her acting debut in _The Mystery of Natalie Wood_, a 2004 television serial directed by Peter Bogdanovich.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-mercury-6) She appeared in a number of American productions – such as the television film _Dynasty: The Making of a Guilty Pleasure_ (2005) (where she played Catherine Oxenberg),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-Dynasty-7)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-mercury-6) and the horror movies_Man-Thing_ (2005) and _See No Evil_ (2006).
Taylor played Sasha Forbes on the short-lived Australian drama series _headLand_. On 3 April 2006, she was nominated for a Logie Award for Most Popular New Female Talent for her role on _headLand_.
Taylor at the premiere of _Transformers_ in Sydney, 2007
Her most prominent role to date was as Maggie Madsen, a signals analyst, in the 2007 _Transformers_, where she appeared alongside Shia LaBeouf and Megan Fox. Taylor confirmed that she would not be returning for the _Transformers_ sequel.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-8) In 2008, Taylor scored a starring role in the US horror-thriller _Shutter_, a remake of the 2004 Thai film of the same name opposite Joshua Jackson.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-9) Despite mixed reviews, the film was a box-office success.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-10)

In 2009, she completed the Australian feature _Cedar Boys_ and starred in the comedy _Splinterheads_. In 2010, she starred alongside Alex Dimitriades in the Australian romantic drama _Summer Coda_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-11) She has also signed to the HBO comedy series _Washingtonienne_ and _Melt_, an Australian production. Taylor began a recurring role on _[Grey's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey's\_Anatomy "Grey's Anatomy")_ as [Dr. Lucy Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Grey's_Anatomy_characters#Attending_physicians "List of Grey's Anatomy characters"), an obstetrician and maternal-fetal fellow.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-14)
In 2011, Taylor joined the cast of the short-lived remake of the television series _[Charlie's Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie's\_Angels\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Charlie's Angels (2011 TV series)")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-16) Also in 2011, she had a major role in the film _Red Dog_ and starred in the Russian science-fiction thriller film _The Darkest Hour_, directed by filmmaker Chris Gorak.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachael_Taylor#cite_note-17)

**Laura Haddock** (born 1985) is a British actress. She is known for portraying Alison in _The Inbetweeners Movie_, Zoë Walker in _White Lines_, Max Meladze in _The Recruit_, Lucrezia in _[Da Vinci's Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da\_Vinci's\_Demons "Da Vinci's Demons")_, Meredith Quill in _Guardians of the Galaxy_ and its sequel _Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2_, and Viviane Wembly in _Transformers: The Last Knight_.

## Early life and education
[edit]
Laura Haddock was born in 1985[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-1) in Enfield, London, to a reflexologist mother and a financier father.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-2) She was raised in Harpenden, Hertfordshire.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-Times1-3)
She attended [St George's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_George's_School,_Harpenden "St George's School, Harpenden") in Harpenden.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-Times1-3) She left school at the age of 17 and moved to London to study drama. She trained at Arts Educational School in Chiswick.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-OK1-4)
Haddock made her television debut in the television pilot_Plus One_, part of the Comedy Showcase 2008.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-5) In 2009, Haddock played the lead role of Natasha in the ITV1comedy drama_Monday Monday_, and appeared as Samantha in series two and three of _How Not to Live Your Life_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-ITV1-6)

## Early life and education
In 2011, she appeared in the Cinemax/Sky TV drama _Strike Back: Project Dawn_ for two episodes, as the kidnapped daughter of an illegal arms dealer. She starred as Lucrezia Donati,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-Cast-7) the mistress of [Lorenzo de' Medici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenzo_de'_Medici "Lorenzo de' Medici") and lover of Leonardo da Vinci in the 2013 series _[Da Vinci's Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da\_Vinci's\_Demons "Da Vinci's Demons")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-8) She played Alison, Will McKenzie's love interest, in _The Inbetweeners Movie_ (2011),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-9) for which she was nominated for the Empire Award for Best Female Newcomer.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-10)
Haddock's theatre credits include _Famous Last_, which formed part of the 2009 Sky Arts Theatre Live! project,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-SkyArts-11) and _Rutherford & Son_ at Northern Stage.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-WOS1-12) In 2014, she portrayed Meredith Quill in _Guardians of the Galaxy_, a role she reprised in its 2017 sequel _Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2_. She appears in the ITV series, _The Level_, and played Vivian Wembley in the 2017 film _Transformers: The Last Knight_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-13)

## Early life and education
In 2021, Haddock starred in a Christmas marketing campaign for British furniture and home accessories retailer OKA.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-ver1-14) In 2022, she starred as Maxine Meladze in the Netflix spy-adventure television series _The Recruit_.
Haddock married English actor Sam Claflin in July 2013 after dating for two years.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-15) They have a son and a daughter.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-16) On 20 August 2019, Haddock and Claflin announced their legal separation.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Haddock#cite_note-18)

### Activator Mini-Cons
[edit]
The **Activators** are a type of Mini-Con who can empower a host in vehicle mode, enabling them with flight capabilities and other enhancements.
*   **Stuntwing** - An Activator Mini-Con employed by Soundwave to steal Bumblebee's Decepticon Hunter.  
*   **Trickout** - An Activator Mini-Con with wheels for feet employed by Soundwave to retrieve a Decepticon Hunter.  
*   **Hi-Test** - An Activator Mini-Con employed by Soundwave to retrieve a Decepticon Hunter. Hi-Test fails to do so and flees from Soundwave to avoid being killed. After Soundwave is defeated, Hi-Test departs to the Shadowzone, where he is able to live without fear of being hunted.  
*   **Goldgear** - An Activator Mini-Con who is employed by Soundwave to retrieve Strongarm's Decepticon Hunter.

### Activator Mini-Cons
*   **Russell Clay** (voiced by Stuart Allan) - A 10-year-old boy who was sent by his mother to live with his father, Denny. He first encounters Sideswipe which leads him and his father to befriend the Autobots. He is headstrong and constantly begs to join the team on their missions. He is also an avid watcher of horror movies. His father often gives him the nickname "Rusty". Russell has shown he can learn from the Autobots and he becomes a valuable member of the team, alongside his father Denny.  
*   **Denny Clay** (voiced by Ted McGinley) - Russell's father who own a scrapyard of collectible items which becomes the Autobot's base of operations. He is also handy with tools and construction which allows him to work alongside Fixit, who in turn allows him to study Cybertronian technology. He also runs interference with the Autobots, using several disguises to help prevent other humans from discovering the Autobot's and Decepticon's existence. Denny tries to be a good father for Russell but does encounter problems. The Autobots, mainly Bumblebee and Fixit, help him overcome these problems. Overall, Denny & Russell become valuable members of the Bee Team.|  
*   **Henrietta "Hank"** (voiced by Bailey Gambertoglio) - A neighborhood girl whom Russell befriends while trying to find others to socialize. She is a fan of football and plays it along with her other friends, including Russell.  
*   **Butch** (voiced by Will Friedle) - A neighborhood boy whom Russell befriends while trying to find others to socialize.  
*   **Larry LaRue** (voiced by John Katovsich) - A greedy collector who will stop at nothing to obtain various items. He apparently has a history with Denny.  
*   **Arnold** (voiced by Troy Baker in "As the Kospego Commands!," James Arnold Taylor in "Suspended") - A man who believes in mythological creatures.

### Activator Mini-Cons
[edit]
The **Activators** are a type of Mini-Con who can empower a host in vehicle mode, enabling them with flight capabilities and other enhancements.
*   **Stuntwing** - An Activator Mini-Con employed by Soundwave to steal Bumblebee's Decepticon Hunter.  
*   **Trickout** - An Activator Mini-Con with wheels for feet employed by Soundwave to retrieve a Decepticon Hunter.  
*   **Hi-Test** - An Activator Mini-Con employed by Soundwave to retrieve a Decepticon Hunter. Hi-Test fails to do so and flees from Soundwave to avoid being killed. After Soundwave is defeated, Hi-Test departs to the Shadowzone, where he is able to live without fear of being hunted.  
*   **Goldgear** - An Activator Mini-Con who is employed by Soundwave to retrieve Strongarm's Decepticon Hunter.

### Activator Mini-Cons
*   **Russell Clay** (voiced by Stuart Allan) - A 10-year-old boy who was sent by his mother to live with his father, Denny. He first encounters Sideswipe which leads him and his father to befriend the Autobots. He is headstrong and constantly begs to join the team on their missions. He is also an avid watcher of horror movies. His father often gives him the nickname "Rusty". Russell has shown he can learn from the Autobots and he becomes a valuable member of the team, alongside his father Denny.  
*   **Denny Clay** (voiced by Ted McGinley) - Russell's father who own a scrapyard of collectible items which becomes the Autobot's base of operations. He is also handy with tools and construction which allows him to work alongside Fixit, who in turn allows him to study Cybertronian technology. He also runs interference with the Autobots, using several disguises to help prevent other humans from discovering the Autobot's and Decepticon's existence. Denny tries to be a good father for Russell but does encounter problems. The Autobots, mainly Bumblebee and Fixit, help him overcome these problems. Overall, Denny & Russell become valuable members of the Bee Team.|  
*   **Henrietta "Hank"** (voiced by Bailey Gambertoglio) - A neighborhood girl whom Russell befriends while trying to find others to socialize. She is a fan of football and plays it along with her other friends, including Russell.  
*   **Butch** (voiced by Will Friedle) - A neighborhood boy whom Russell befriends while trying to find others to socialize.  
*   **Larry LaRue** (voiced by John Katovsich) - A greedy collector who will stop at nothing to obtain various items. He apparently has a history with Denny.  
*   **Arnold** (voiced by Troy Baker in "As the Kospego Commands!," James Arnold Taylor in "Suspended") - A man who believes in mythological creatures.

Born February 23, 2000 in Houston, Texas, USA
Bailey Gambertoglio is a voice actor and musician. She has always had a love for entertaining. You might have heard her as the voice of Molly in Nick Jr.'s "Bubble Guppies", Abagail in Netflix's "Spirit Riding Free", Shoka in "Neo: The World Ends With You" and many more roles on various cartoons/video games.
